author: jsign
content:
Closing a bit the loop reg the discussion above since we had a team call earlier today.

Technically, with the [R2 bucket](https://pub-760ad8b3dd9547539f829c1ea30f18b5.r2.dev/devnets/glamsterdam-devnet-8/index.html) we announced some days ago, we can already prove any historical devnet-8 block. This means we can start at least trying to see how 200M gas limit related to proving using EF proving cluster... so this means doesn't technically need explicit "devnet participation" on that front.

Might still be questionable if the workload from devnet-8 or sepolia is representative for proving time perf; since the kind of workload there might not be comparable to mainnet...
Eventually, we'll have Glamsterdam mainnet which would be the main "avg case" target; but agree with above comments proving 200M blocks on these devnet/testnet is useful. Just noting that we can do if "offline" with the R2 bucket. (we have been doing this for devnet-7 actually).

Still, joining devnet-8 or sepolia can be interesting for other useful/important reasons:
1. More e2e testing of zkboost in a live network, instead of "offline proving" with the R2 bucket.
2. At some point would be interesting to explore CL block building having proving support. This basically means pipelining executionWitness construction in the block builder, compared to the offline proving where the executionWitness requires re-execution which add some extra "lag time" that in theory doesn't make sense long-term (i.e. mandatory proofs). This isn't strictly related to 8025 since block builders aren't creating proofs; but still a useful part of the proving pipeline for mandatory proofs.
3. Might be more motivating for zkVM teams to join a live devnet/testnet to test on their proving hw or forked-guest programs where they experiment with stuff -- but we could wait for the right moment to ask them to do that.
